neighbours.label: the verb 'has/have' right after a pronoun subject in a running clause ('it has to', 'they have dinner'), as possessive or semi-modal
fire: If the printer jams again, it has to be sent back to the shop.
Ask the seller whether it has a warranty before you pay.
On Sundays the twins visit their aunt, and they have lunch on her porch.
The car is old, but it has a new engine and good tyres.
When students finish early, they have time to read in the library.
Before the meeting starts, check that it has a clear agenda.
Once you pass the exam, you have the right to practise.
The kettle is cheap, yet it has an automatic shut-off switch.
quiet: If the printer jams again, it goes back to the shop.
Ask the seller whether it works before you pay.
On Sundays the twins visit their aunt, and they eat lunch on her porch.
The car is old, but it runs well on new tyres.
When students finish early, they read in the library.
Before the meeting starts, check that it follows a clear agenda.
Once you pass the exam, you can start to practise.
The kettle is cheap, yet it switches off automatically.
